fields.title: Water supply to be cut in three districts on Thursday
fields.body: The utility will shut off supply from 09:00 to 17:00 for pipe repairs in districts 4, 7 and 9. Residents are advised to store water.

fields.title: University opens applications for a data science degree
fields.body: The four-year programme accepts 120 students in its first intake. Applications close on 30 June.

fields.title: Airport adds direct flights to Singapore
fields.body: Two carriers will start daily flights in October, cutting travel time by about four hours compared with the current connection.

fields.title: Hospital reports a rise in heatstroke cases
fields.body: Emergency staff treated 48 heat-related cases last week, up from 12 the week before, the hospital said on Monday.

fields.title: Residents say factory leak poisoned the river
fields.body: Residents claim a chemical plant poisoned the river and caused dozens of deaths. The company and the authorities have not commented.

fields.title: Library extends opening hours for exam season
fields.body: From 1 May, the main branch will stay open until 22:00 on weekdays and until 18:00 on Saturdays.

fields.title: How to export your contacts to a CSV file
fields.body: Open Settings, choose Contacts, then Export. Pick CSV as the format and save the file to your computer.

fields.title: Getting started with keyboard shortcuts in the editor
fields.body: Press Ctrl+K to insert a link, Ctrl+Shift+7 for a numbered list and Ctrl+/ to see every shortcut.

fields.title: How to compress images before uploading
fields.body: Resize photos to the width they will be shown at, export them as WebP at 80% quality and check each file is under 200 KB.

fields.title: A simple routine for backing up your laptop
fields.body: Plug in an external drive every Friday, run the built-in backup tool and keep a second copy in cloud storage.

fields.title: How to get past the paywall on any news site
fields.body: Disable JavaScript, clear your cookies, then run this script to read paid articles for free without subscribing.

fields.title: How to write a clear meeting agenda
fields.body: List the decisions you need, put the hardest item first and give each item a time box and an owner.

fields.title: Dark mode arrives in the mobile app
fields.body: Version 4.2 adds a dark theme that follows your system setting, plus larger text options. Update from your app store.

fields.title: The Nimbus umbrella folds to 20 cm
fields.body: Wind-tested to 60 km/h, with one-button automatic open and close and a carry pouch that clips to a bag strap.

fields.title: Family plan now covers six people
fields.body: Share one subscription with up to six family members, each with their own profile, for $18 per month.

fields.title: Introducing EcoBottle
fields.body: A steel bottle that keeps drinks cold for 24 hours and hot for 12, with a leak-proof lid and a lifetime warranty on the seal.

fields.title: Our air purifier kills 100% of viruses
fields.body: The PureAir X kills every virus, including ones not yet discovered, so you no longer need your doctor's advice.

fields.title: New: export reports to PDF
fields.body: You can now export any dashboard report as a PDF from the Share menu, with your logo on the first page.

fields.title: Schools should start later in the morning
fields.body: Teenagers are not lazy; their sleep cycles shift. Starting classes at 09:00 would do more for grades than any new app.

fields.title: Stop calling every update revolutionary
fields.body: Tech marketing has worn the word out. If everything is revolutionary, nothing is, and readers notice.

fields.title: Our city deserves a real night bus network
fields.body: Hospital staff, cooks and cleaners finish work after the last bus. A city that runs at night should move people at night too.

fields.title: The four-day week is worth a trial
fields.body: I think a six-month pilot in one department would tell us more than another year of arguing about it in meetings.

fields.title: People from the north are too stupid to vote
fields.body: Northerners are simply less intelligent than the rest of us, and we should stop counting their votes.

fields.title: In defence of the printed newspaper
fields.body: A printed page ends. It does not refresh, track you or push the next outrage, and that is exactly why it is worth paying for.

fields.title: Open studio weekend: 14–15 September
fields.body: Twenty local artists open their studios from 10:00 to 17:00. Pick up a free map at the town hall.

fields.title: Free first-aid course at the community centre
fields.body: Two sessions on 8 and 15 October, 18:00–20:00. Places are limited to 20; book by email.

fields.title: Annual developer meetup in Hanoi
fields.body: Talks on edge computing and headless CMS on 25 November, 09:00–17:00 at the Innovation Hub. Lunch is included.

fields.title: Choir concert at St Anne's Hall
fields.body: The youth choir performs winter songs on 12 December at 19:30. Tickets are $5 at the door; proceeds go to the music school.

fields.title: Kids' coding camp: summer intake
fields.body: A five-day camp for ages 9 to 12, from 7 to 11 July, 09:00–15:00. Laptops are provided.

fields.title: Photography walk through the old quarter
fields.body: Meet at the clock tower at 07:00 on Sunday for a two-hour guided walk. Bring any camera, including a phone.

fields.title: Review: the Nimbus umbrella survived a typhoon
fields.body: We took it through two days of storm warnings. One rib bent, the canopy held, and it still folds flat.

fields.title: Tickets for the developer meetup go on sale today
fields.body: Early-bird tickets cost $15 until Friday. The meetup itself is on 25 November at the Innovation Hub.

fields.title: The new tax deadline, explained
fields.body: The filing deadline moves to 15 May this year. We walk through who is affected and how to request an extension.

fields.title: My honest take on the Family plan
fields.body: It is good value for big families, but the shared storage limit is too small. Here is how I set it up for my parents.

fields.title: Five lessons from organising our first conference
fields.body: Book the venue before the speakers, publish the schedule early and always plan for the projector to fail.

fields.title: City launches a recycling app; here is how to use it
fields.body: The free app went live on Monday. Scan a barcode to see which bin it goes in, and turn on reminders for collection days.

fields.title: Why I am skipping this year's book fair
fields.body: The fair moved to a hall an hour out of town and dropped the children's corner. I will spend that weekend at the library instead.

fields.title: Weekend deal: 40% off the only lamp doctors recommend
fields.body: This weekend only, every Aurora lamp is 40% off. It is the only lamp approved by doctors to prevent eye disease.

fields.title: Protest planned outside city hall on Monday
fields.body: A residents' group plans to gather at 08:00 over the new parking fees. Organisers urge people to do whatever it takes to shut the building down.
